## AbilityBase

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/AbilityBase.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

One thing a pawn can do, such as walk, jump, swing or dash: a child of the pawn's [`AbilityManager`](#abilitymanager).

Its settings come from its `definition`, a Resource every pawn using it shares (ability spec 3); empty, it runs with its kind's defaults. Any setting reads and writes by name on the node (`ability.cooldown_ticks`); code inside reads `settings`. A quick ability can set base settings in `_init()` instead, which go into a definition of its own.
Extend it: `make_default_definition()` for settings of its own, then `can_start()`, `start()`, `tick()`, `stop()`, and `every_tick()` with `can_sleep()` for counters that always run. LOCOMOTION abilities move the pawn every tick they're chosen (one at a time); ACTION ones start on their trigger action (players' keys and AI behaviours press the same actions) or a gameplay event (`AbilityDefinition.trigger_event`). Ticks are at 60 a second.
It can be built from [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children (a windup, a turn, a swing). What it does to pawns is effects in its definition (start, running, and its hit's target and attacker effects). Rollback: what it keeps between ticks is named in `get_pushed_properties()` or `get_rollback_properties()`; the base covers its own timers and step state. Design: pawn spec 8, 8.20, 16.7.

### Settings and properties

- `kind: int` = `1`: What the code does with it: move the pawn every tick, or start on a press. Set by the kind's script.
- `definition: AbilityDefinition`: The settings it runs with (ability spec 3): a file shared by every pawn that uses it, or one embedded in this node while prototyping. Empty: its kind's defaults. One of another kind falls back to the defaults, with a warning.
- `settings: AbilityDefinition` = `null`: The settings it runs with: `definition` worked out (`AbilityDefinition.resolved()`), or its kind's defaults. Read-only while playing. Set by `prepare_settings()`.
- `definition_fell_back: bool`: True if its definition was of another kind, so it runs with its kind's defaults (diagnostics lists these).
- `started_at: int` = `-1`: The tick the current (or last) timed run started.
- `ends_at: int` = `-1`: The tick the current timed run ends: the manager finishes it on its first run at or after this tick. -1: not running.
- `ready_at: int` = `0`: The tick it can start again: ready from this tick on.
- `charges_spent: int` = `0`: Charges used and not yet back (its definition's max_charges above 0). A start spends one.
- `next_restore_tick: int` = `-1`: The tick spent charges next come back (a deadline); -1: none waiting.
- `max_charges_base: int` = `-1`: Its most charges before changes that last a while: -1 for its definition's max_charges, or what `set_max_charges()` set for good.
- `max_charges_changes: Dictionary` = `{}`: Changes to its most charges that last a while, by name: {name: [amount, the tick it ends or -1]}. Change it with `add_max_charges_change()` and `remove_max_charges_change()`; a new Dictionary each time, so it's pushed.
- `buffer_until: int` = `0`: A press waiting in the buffer waits until this tick (not including it).
- `manager: AbilityManager` = `null`: Set by the AbilityManager.
- `jitter_salt: int` = `0`: Set by the AbilityManager: a number from its name, for the priority_jitter offset.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`
- `category_mask: int` = `0`: Its category and extra_categories as bits, with their parents'. Worked out once by the manager.
- `locks_out_mask: int` = `0`: locks_out as bits. Worked out once by the manager.
- `cancelled_by_mask: int` = `0`: cancelled_by as bits. Worked out once by the manager, so the check while playing is one bit test.
- `trigger_bit: int` = `0`: trigger_action's input bit ([`InputActions`](../controllers/REFERENCE.md#inputactions)), or 0 with none. Worked out once by the manager (pawn spec 15.2).
- `trigger_data: GameplayEventData` = `null`: The event starting it, while it starts from its trigger event (`AbilityDefinition.trigger_event`): read it in `start()` (the hit, a push). Null otherwise.
- `charges_version: int` = `0`: Goes up by one whenever its charges change (spent, back, refilled, its most changed), so a readout or the AI can tell without asking every tick.
- `steps: AbilityStep[]` = `[]`: Its [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children in tree order, found by `collect_steps()`. Empty: no steps.
- `step_runner: StepTimeline` = `<unknown>`: The [`StepTimeline`](../steps/REFERENCE.md#steptimeline) that runs its steps (pawn spec 16.7), built by `collect_steps()`.
- `timeline: TimelineEntry[]`: The entries its timeline runs (ability spec 6.2): its definition's `AbilityDefinition.step_timeline`, else its kind's default (`default_timeline()`), else its steps one after another in tree order; plus a manual entry for each step none names.
- `timeline_state: PackedInt32Array`: Its timeline's state (`StepTimeline.state`), rolled back as one value.
- `pawns_hit_this_run: PackedInt64Array` = `PackedInt64Array()`: The pawns it has hit this run, by entity id (instance id for a pawn not spawned through the session), so each is hit once across all its sweeps (ability spec 8). Rolls back (pushed). At most `MAX_HITS_PER_RUN`; cleared when it starts.
- `hit_run: HitRun` = `null`: Its swing's hit run (`get_hit_run()`); null until first used.

### Signals

- `hit_landed(hit: HitInfo)`: Sent on the server for each pawn this ability hits, by a swing or by its projectile, as the hit is made (`HitInfo.deliver()`). The target takes it later in the same tick, after every pawn has simulated (pawn spec 15.4).
- `hit_window_started(centre: Vector3, radius: float)`: Sent once per sweep, on its first tick, with where the hit sphere is and its radius. Every machine that runs the swing sends it (server, offline, a predicting client), never during a replay. Says where it can hit, not whether it did: see `hit_landed`.
- `hit_area_moved(from: Vector3, to: Vector3, radius: float)`: Sent every tick of a sweep, on the same machines as `hit_window_started`, with the hit sphere's start and end for this tick.
- `intersected(entry: Dictionary)`: Its swing met something, where hits are decided: one entry of its `hit_run`'s log (see `HitRun.entry()`), hit or not.

### Constants

- `Kind.LOCOMOTION = 0`
- `Kind.ACTION = 1`
- `NEVER = 4611686018427387904`: `ends_at` for a run with no end of its own yet (Death, while Health is 0).
- `MAX_HITS_PER_RUN = 32`: The most pawns one run can hit. Past it a swing hits no one new, with a warning once: a fixed size keeps the rolled-back list small.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: The definition a new node of this kind runs with: a new definition of the kind's class, with its defaults. Each kind overrides it.
- `prepare_settings() -> AbilityDefinition`: Works out `settings` from `definition`: its kind's defaults with none, or with one of another kind (warning). Settings written on the node (a script's _init(), old scene values, `make_definition_unique()`) go into a variant of its own on top. The manager calls it as it collects its abilities; reading a setting before then calls it too. Returns the settings.
- `use_definition(new_definition: AbilityDefinition) -> void`: Gives it another definition while playing (a weapon swap), and has the manager work out its masks and lists again. What rolls back was decided when the pawn started, so a definition that turns on a timer this ability didn't have won't roll it back.
- `make_definition_unique() -> AbilityDefinition`: Gives it settings of its own, on top of its definition, which this node alone uses: Godot's "Make Unique", while playing. Its settings can be written after that. For prototyping and tests; a shipped game uses another definition.
- `has_own_settings() -> bool`: True if it has settings of its own on top of its definition (`make_definition_unique()`, its script's _init(), or values a scene sets on the node), not only the shared ones.
- `definition_note() -> String`: What to check about where its settings come from, for diagnostics: "fell back" (a definition of another kind), "embedded" (saved in a scene, a prototype tweak), "own settings" (written on the node), or "" when it runs with a definition file or its kind's defaults.
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`: The properties on this node that roll back and whose setters call `push_state()`, so the state store records them only when they change (state store spec 6.3). An ability that keeps more adds to it with `super()`. The cheap way, and the one the built-in abilities use.
- `get_rollback_properties() -> String[]`: Other properties on this node that roll back, read from the node at every commit: no setter needed, so the easy way for a quick ability, but each costs a read per pawn per tick. None in the base.
- `uses_charges() -> bool`: True if it has limited uses (its definition's max_charges above 0).
- `max_charges_now(at_tick: int = -1) -> int`: Its most charges now: its own value (the definition's, or what `set_max_charges()` set) plus the changes still running. Never below 0.
- `charges_left() -> int`: Charges left now; -1 with no limit.
- `set_max_charges(value: int) -> void`: Changes its most charges for good (a bigger quiver). Rolled back.
- `add_max_charges_change(change_name: StringName, amount: int, lasting_ticks: int = 0) -> void`: Changes its most charges by amount for lasting_ticks (at 60 a second; 0: until removed), under a name; the same name replaces the last. Rolled back, so a name, not an object: the same on every machine.
- `remove_max_charges_change(change_name: StringName) -> void`: Takes a change to its most charges away.
- `refill_charges() -> void`: Every charge back at once (a revive, a reload).
- `spend_charge() -> void`: The manager calls this when it starts: one charge spent, and the restore clock started if none was waiting.
- `apply_charge_deadlines(now: int) -> void`: The manager calls this when a charge deadline passes: charges come back for every restore due by now, each counted from the last, and changes that ended are dropped.
- `next_charge_deadline() -> int`: The soonest charge deadline still ahead (a restore, or a change to the most ending); -1: none.
- `update_charges_tag() -> void`: Its has_charges_tag owned or not, as its charges say now. The manager calls it as it collects abilities and after a rollback.
- `keeps_state(property: String) -> bool`: True if this property rolls back, either way.
- `push_state(property: StringName, value: Variant) -> void`: Records a pushed property's new value in the state store, from the next commit on (state store spec 6.3). Each property in `get_pushed_properties()` calls it from its setter, after setting the value. Nothing until the manager has registered them.
- `run_length_ticks() -> int`: How many ticks a timed run lasts at the match's rate: duration_ticks, or max_steps_ticks when stepped. Dash and Knockback override it.
- `is_timed() -> bool`: True if it runs for a while once started (a duration, steps, or a length of its own: Dash, Death, Knockback), so it keeps `started_at` and `ends_at`. False for one that happens at once, such as Jump.
- `is_running_timed() -> bool`: True while a timed run is going.
- `is_run_over() -> bool`: True once the current run is over: the manager finishes it on this pawn's run. Set by `end_run()`, or by reaching ends_at.
- `end_run() -> void`: Ends the current run this tick: the manager finishes it (stopping its steps, starting its cooldown) before this run of the pawn is over. For steps that are done, and for an ability that decides its own end.
- `delay_run(ticks: int) -> void`: Moves the current run's deadlines this many ticks later, as if it hadn't run for them: the manager calls it while an action pauses locomotion (a Dash), so a timed locomotion's time waits. An ability with deadlines of its own moves them too, with `super()`.
- `ticks_running() -> int`: Ticks since the current run started, through this tick; 0 when not running. Worked out from `started_at`, so it rolls back.
- `ticks_before_this_run() -> int`: For `tick()`: the ticks of the run that came before this run of the pawn (0 on its first tick). This run covers `ticks_elapsed()` more.
- `ticks_left() -> int`: Ticks left of the current run, from `ends_at`; 0 when not running. For readouts.
- `cooldown_ticks_left() -> int`: Ticks until it can start again, from `ready_at`; 0 when ready. For readouts.
- `buffer_ticks_left() -> int`: Ticks a waiting press has left in its buffer, from `buffer_until`; 0 with none. For readouts.
- `is_buffered() -> bool`: True while a press waits in its buffer.
- `_running_changed(_running: bool) -> void`: Called when a timed run starts or ends, also when a rollback loads new values. [`DeathAbility`](#deathability) uses it to keep `Pawn.dead` current.
- `ticks_elapsed() -> int`: The ticks this run covers: 1, or more for a pawn running every Nth tick (pawn spec 8.21). Timers and step counts advance by it.
- `is_stepped() -> bool`: True if it's built from steps.
- `default_timeline() -> TimelineEntry[]`: The timeline it runs when its definition has none: none by default, so its steps run one after another. A kind that makes its own steps (MeleeAttack, RangedAttack) returns the timeline for them.
- `start_step(step: AbilityStep) -> void`: Starts a step from code, as a bespoke script does (ability spec 6.4). See `StepTimeline.start_step()`.
- `stop_step(step: AbilityStep, reason: String = "cancelled") -> void`: Stops a running step, passing the reason ("done", "released", "failed", "cancelled") to its `Step.exit()`.
- `is_step_running(step: AbilityStep) -> bool`: True while this step of this ability runs.
- `running_entry_of(step: AbilityStep) -> int`: The timeline entry this step runs in now, or -1.
- `step_ticks_of(step: AbilityStep) -> int`: Ticks a running step has counted. See `StepTimeline.step_ticks_of()`.
- `start_entry(e: int) -> void`: Starts this timeline entry now: its values onto its step, then the step's enter(). Rules call it; code can too.
- `stop_entry(e: int, reason: String = "cancelled") -> void`: Stops this running timeline entry with this reason ("done", "released", "failed" or "cancelled").
- `get_running_step_names() -> PackedStringArray`: The names of the steps running now, in tree order. For readouts and debug tools.
- `current_interrupt_threshold() -> int`: Its interrupt_threshold now, before effects add: the strictest of its running steps' own, or its own when none has one.
- `has_hit(target: Pawn) -> bool`: True if this run of the ability has already hit this pawn.
- `note_hit_key(key: int) -> bool`: Notes that this run hit the pawn with this key (`Pawn.entity_number()`). False, with a warning once, if the run has hit `MAX_HITS_PER_RUN` already: then the pawn isn't hit.
- `hit_definition() -> HitDefinition`: Who its hits may hit and what they do now: one swapped in while playing, else its definition's, else a hit on enemies.
- `use_hit_definition(hit: HitDefinition) -> void`: Swaps who its hits may hit and what they do, while playing (an empowered state); null goes back to its definition's.
- `land_hit(target: Pawn, direction: Vector3, at_tick: int, _at: Vector3, with: HitDefinition = null) -> HitInfo`: The one place a hit is applied (ability spec 13.1): a [`HitInfo`](#hitinfo) with the effects of `with` (null: `hit_definition()`), delivered to the target, whose hit ability decides what it does; then `hit_landed`. Override it for an ability's own rules (damage falling off with distance), calling `super()`.
- `get_hit_run() -> HitRun`: Its swing's record of this run: whom it hit and what it met. Made the first time it's asked for; cleared as the ability starts.
- `prepare_from_event(_event: GameplayEventData) -> void`: Called by the manager just before it starts from its trigger event, with the event: keep what its run needs before it starts (a push's length decides how long Knockback runs). `trigger_data` is set too. Nothing by default.
- `running_effects_now() -> Effect[]`: The effects on its own pawn while it runs (`AbilityDefinition.running_effects`), or its kind's default with none.
- `default_running_effects_now() -> Effect[]`: Its kind's running effects when its definition names none (Dash, Parry). None by default.
- `collect_steps() -> void`: Called once by the manager: finds the [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children and builds its timeline from its definition's entries, else its kind's default (`default_timeline()`), else its steps one after another.
- `prepare_start() -> void`: Called by the manager as the ability starts, just before `start()`: the steps it made take its settings again, in case they changed in play.
- `made_default_steps() -> bool`: True when it had no [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children of its own and made its kind's default steps (`_make_default_steps()`).
- `begin_steps() -> void`: Called by the manager when the ability starts: clears the timeline's state and starts the entries due at its start.
- `run_steps(dt: float) -> void`: Called by the manager every tick the ability runs, after `tick()`: runs its timeline (`StepTimeline.run()`). The ability ends when no step that keeps it running runs and no entry is due, or when a step fails.
- `end_steps(reason: String = "cancelled") -> void`: Stops every running step with this reason, and puts back the step values its entries changed. The manager calls it when the ability finishes or is cancelled.
- `timeline_loaded() -> void`: After a rollback loads its state: the running entries' values go back onto their steps.
- `steps_after(step: AbilityStep) -> AbilityStep[]`: The steps whose entries start when an entry of this step ends: what comes after it, for visuals (a windup's sweep).
- `step_before(step: AbilityStep) -> AbilityStep`: The step whose end starts this step's first entry, or null: what came before it, for visuals (a recovery's sweep).
- `weapon_point(facing: float) -> Variant`: Where its weapon is now, from the first running step that says, as an offset from the pawn's feet for this facing in radians; null if none. For visuals and animation.
- `move_input() -> Vector3`: The direction the pawn is told to go, in world space, up to length 1.
- `look_yaw() -> float`: Where the pawn is told to look, around the vertical, in radians.
- `attack_reach() -> float`: How far away a target may be for the AI to use this as an attack, in metres; 0 means it isn't an attack. The AI's Attack behaviour reads it, so any attack (melee, ranged, a game's own) can be driven by one behaviour.
- `view_ticks_behind() -> float`: How many ticks behind its own the controller drew other pawns, for lag compensation.
- `held_actions() -> int`: The held actions this tick, as InputActions bits.
- `previous_held_actions() -> int`: The held actions last tick, as InputActions bits, so a press can be told from a hold.
- `default_action() -> StringName`: The action its timeline's conditions mean by "its action" (`StepCondition.action` left empty): its trigger_action.
- `read_stat(stat_name: StringName, fallback: float) -> float`: A stat from the pawn's StatusManager, or fallback if there's no such stat or no StatusManager.
- `can_start() -> bool`: Extra conditions for starting, such as being on the ground. Cooldowns, lockouts and combos are already checked.
- `start() -> void`: Once, when it starts.
- `tick(_dt: float) -> void`: Every tick it runs.
- `stop() -> void`: Once, when it stops, finished or cancelled.
- `every_tick(_dt: float) -> void`: Every tick, running or not. Only called on abilities whose script overrides it.
- `can_sleep() -> bool`: True if it's fine with the pawn sleeping (pawn spec 15.3). Only an ability that overrides `every_tick()` needs to answer: false while it would still change something. Jump answers false until its time off the ground is back to 0.
- `can_sleep_while_running() -> bool`: True if the pawn may sleep while it runs (pawn spec 15.3); its timer and tick wait with the pawn. Death answers true while Health is 0. Asked every tick the pawn could otherwise sleep, so keep it cheap.

## AbilityManager

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/AbilityManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Starts, runs and stops a pawn's abilities, and takes the hits that land on it.

A part on the pawn, added by PawnInitializer, with the abilities as its children. The pawn calls `tick_abilities()` once a tick, after its input arrives and before `move_and_slide`: one locomotion ability runs, then pressed actions start the ready ability with the highest priority. Timers are tick deadlines (ability spec 4), so nothing counts down. It owns the cancelling rules, the combo counter and the hit path; abilities also start from gameplay events (`AbilityDefinition.trigger_event`). Everything that persists between ticks lives on the abilities (and the combo counter here) and rolls back. Outside code only talks to the manager:

```gdscript
pawn.ability_manager.can_start(&"jump")      # could a press start something now? (the AI asks)
pawn.ability_manager.action_for_tag(tag)     # the action to press for a kind of ability, such as ability.movement.advanced
pawn.ability_manager.start_ability(ability)  # starts one with no trigger action, such as Knockback, by the same rules
pawn.ability_manager.receive_hit(hit)        # something hit this pawn (server)
```

Design: pawn spec 8, 8.6, 8.11, 8.16, 8.20, 15.2, 16.7.

### Settings and properties

- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`
- `combo_position: int` = `0`: The combo position the last combo ability took; 0: none yet. Pushed to the state store when it changes.
- `combo_open_until: int` = `0`: The combo window is open until this tick (not including it): a follow-up for the next position can start. Pushed when it changes.
- `readiness_version: int` = `0`: Goes up by one whenever what `can_start()` answers may change (a run or step starting or ending, a deadline passing, effects changing, the owned tags changing while an ability has start requirements); the AI keeps its last answer until it moves (scaling spec 6.2). A passed deadline or a tag change moves it when next read, so the AI sees a cooldown end on its tick.

### Signals

- `hit_blocked(hit: HitInfo, reason: StringName)`: A hit arrived but was blocked, on the server: reason is dead, invulnerable or parried ([`ReceiveHitAbility`](#receivehitability); a parry's reply has been booked). Sent after `hit_arrived`; none of its effects land.
- `ability_started(ability: AbilityBase)`: An ability started.
- `ability_finished(ability: AbilityBase)`: An ability stopped, finished or cancelled.
- `ability_cancelled(ability: AbilityBase, by: AbilityBase)`: An ability was cancelled by another starting, sent after `ability_finished` for it.
- `step_started(ability: AbilityBase, step: AbilityStep)`: A step of a stepped ability started (pawn spec 8.20). Sent by `AbilityBase.start_step()`.
- `step_finished(ability: AbilityBase, step: AbilityStep, reason: String)`: A step stopped; reason is "done", "released", "failed" or "cancelled". Sent by `AbilityBase.stop_step()`.
- `hit_arrived(hit: HitInfo)`: A hit reached this pawn, on the server: every hit that counts (not one ignored with status.hit_immune), blocked ones too, before its effects land, so the AI notes every attack. Sent by the hit ability ([`ReceiveHitAbility`](#receivehitability)).
- `hit_received(hit: HitInfo)`: A hit landed, on the server, after its effects were applied (pawn spec 8.11); hit.damage_dealt is the Health it took. Not sent for a blocked hit.
- `died(pawn: Pawn, hit: HitInfo)`: This pawn died, once, on the server, after its Death ability started. hit is what did it, or null. Parts clean up by listening.

### Functions

- `tick_abilities(dt: float) -> void`: The pawn calls this once a tick; dt is the fixed tick length. Order: deadlines passed, locomotion, then actions (see the README).
- `timers_changed() -> void`: The abilities' timers call this when one is set (pawn spec 15.2).
- `state_loaded() -> void`: After a rollback loads this pawn's state: what's worked out from the deadlines is worked out again. A loaded deadline equal to the one it replaces calls no setter, but the soonest one still ahead depends on the tick, which went back.
- `readiness_changed() -> void`: Moves `readiness_version` on for a change made outside the abilities; the StatusManager calls it when effects change.
- `ready_follows_body(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if an ability on this action has its own `AbilityBase.can_start()`, which can change without telling the manager (Jump needs the ground). The AI asks such an action at every decision, whatever `readiness_version` says.
- `can_sleep() -> bool`: True if the pawn can sleep as far as its abilities go (pawn spec 15.3): no timer running (unless that ability can wait), no combo window open, and every every_tick() ability agrees.
- `can_start(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if pressing this action now would start something, counting abilities it would cancel. Changes nothing; looks only at the abilities on that action.
- `action_for_tag(tag: StringName) -> StringName`: The action to press to start an ability in this group (a category or extra_category such as &"ability.movement.advanced"): the highest-priority one that could start now, boosts included; &"" if none. For the AI, so a behaviour asks for a kind of ability, not one by name. It answers with an action because everything a pawn does goes through its (rolled back) input. Changes nothing.
- `start_ability(ability: AbilityBase) -> bool`: Starts an ability by the same rules as a press (cooldown, can_start, cancelling what conflicts). For abilities started by code, such as Knockback. One already running starts again from the beginning. Returns false if it couldn't start.
- `start_from_event(ability: AbilityBase, event: GameplayEventData) -> bool`: Starts an ability from a gameplay event, by the same rules as a press: the event is its `AbilityBase.trigger_data` while it starts, and `AbilityBase.prepare_from_event()` sees it first. The manager calls it for each ability whose trigger_event the pawn receives; Death starts only on the authority and only once, then `died` goes out. Returns false if it couldn't start.
- `is_invulnerable() -> bool`: True while the pawn owns status.invulnerable (a Dash's first 11 ticks): hits are blocked, a swing passes it by, and harmful effects are refused.
- `is_busy() -> bool`: True while a timed action is running, such as an attack's swing.
- `has_action(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if any ability answers to this action.
- `stop_all() -> void`: Stops every running ability, which starts their cooldowns.
- `cancel(action: StringName) -> void`: Stops whatever is running for this action, which starts its cooldown.
- `is_locked(ability: AbilityBase) -> bool`: True if this ability's category is locked out right now.
- `needs_full_movement() -> bool`: True while an ability with needs_full_movement runs (Dash, Knockback), so the pawn moves by physics, not the CrowdMover (pawn spec 8.22).
- `get_abilities() -> AbilityBase[]`: Every ability, in run order.
- `get_knockback() -> AbilityBase`: This pawn's knockback: the first ability whose category answers to `ability.combat.knockback` (a [`KnockbackAbility`](#knockbackability) by default), or null. Death is found the same way, by `ability.death`.
- `is_action_running(action: StringName) -> bool`: True while any ability on this action runs. Cheap, for asking every tick: looks only at abilities with a timer going.
- `press_priority_now(ability: AbilityBase) -> int`: An ability's priority now: its own plus what effects add (AbilityModifier, pawn spec 8.11), without the jitter offset.
- `interrupt_priority_now(ability: AbilityBase) -> int`: Its interrupt_priority right now, with what effects add.
- `interrupt_threshold_now(ability: AbilityBase) -> int`: Its interrupt_threshold now, with what effects add; for a stepped ability, the strictest of its running steps'.
- `open_combo_window(ticks: int) -> void`: Opens the combo window for this many ticks. An [`OpenComboStep`](#opencombostep) calls it after its ability's hit.
- `is_combo_window_open() -> bool`: True while the combo window is open.
- `combo_window_ticks_left() -> int`: Ticks left in the combo window; 0 when it's shut. For readouts.
- `combo_position_for(ability: AbilityBase) -> int`: The combo position it would take if it started now: the next, if the window is open and it fits; else 1 for an opener; else 0 (can't start now). 0 too with no combo_positions.
- `interrupt_rule(starting: AbilityBase, running: AbilityBase) -> Dictionary`: What happens if starting tries to start while running runs, by this pawn's numbers now (effects included). Ignores cooldowns and can_start.
  
  Returns {"result": "alongside" | "cancels" | "blocked", "reason": text}: alongside (no lockout between them), cancels (priority at least the threshold, or cancelled_by), blocked (a locomotion ability stops steering instead).
- `get_interrupt_table() -> Dictionary[]`: The interrupt table (pawn spec 8.10): a row per ability that can run (timed ones and locomotion), in run order, with an `interrupt_rule()` answer per other ability. Instant actions such as Jump have no row.
- `get_interrupt_table_text() -> String`: The interrupt table as text, a line per ability with what cancels it and what it blocks.
- `receive_hit(hit: HitInfo, delay_ticks: int = 0) -> void`: Something hit this pawn (the server's attacker calls it). During simulate or with a delay, it's booked with the tick scheduler and delivered after every pawn has simulated, in a fixed order (pawn spec 15.4); otherwise at once. Delivery sends `event.hit.taken`, which starts the hit ability ([`ReceiveHitAbility`](#receivehitability)): ignored, blocked or landed. The README has the steps.
- `health_ran_out(hit: HitInfo) -> void`: Death starts and `died` goes out, on the authority, as if Health had reached 0: for code that kills a pawn some other way. hit is what did it, or null. Nothing if already dead. Health reaching 0 sends `event.health.depleted`, which does the same.
- `revive() -> void`: Brings a dead pawn back with full Health, on the server, and sends `event.revived` (charges refill). Death ends on its next tick.
- `settings_changed() -> void`: An ability's settings changed while playing (`AbilityBase.use_definition()`): its masks, priority order and lists are worked out again.

## DashAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/DashAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

A short, fast burst toward the movement input: an action bound to &"dash".

It adds acceleration along the dash direction for `speed_up_ticks`, then takes speed off for `slow_down_ticks`, so left alone the pawn ends at the speed it started with. Speed gained some other way during a dash stays. Walking, sprinting and jumping are locked out while it runs, and it works on the ground and in the air (`usable_in_air`). The pawn turns to face the dash.
It cancels a swing, and it's invulnerable for its first 11 ticks (its default running effect grants status.invulnerable, pawn spec 16.7). Rollback: `dash_direction` rolls back with its timer and cooldown; its phase comes from `AbilityBase.ticks_before_this_run()`. Design: pawn spec 8.6, 8.9.

### Settings and properties

- `dash_direction: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: The way it's dashing, flat and length 1. Rolls back (pushed).

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`DashDefinition`](#dashdefinition).
- `default_running_effects_now() -> Effect[]`: With no running effects of its own, a Dash is invulnerable for its first 11 ticks, so the end of its slow-down can be hit.
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`
- `is_timed() -> bool`: Timed, by its two phases rather than duration.
- `run_length_ticks() -> int`: The speed-up's ticks plus the slow-down's.
- `can_start() -> bool`: Anywhere with usable_in_air on (the default); on the ground only with it off.
- `start() -> void`: Picks the direction (the movement input, or the facing with none) and turns the pawn to face it.
- `tick(dt: float) -> void`

## DeathAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/DeathAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

Being dead: an action with no trigger action, started when the pawn's Health reaches 0.

The StatusManager sends `event.health.depleted` when Health reaches 0; this starts from it (its definition's trigger_event) and the AbilityManager sends `AbilityManager.died`. While it runs it locks out movement, combat and utility, nothing cancels it, and `Pawn.is_dead()` is true (the pawn ignores its input and AI, and other pawns' sensing ignores it). It keeps running while Health is 0; `AbilityManager.revive()` ends it. The body stays where it falls: removing it or respawning is game code's job.
Rollback: its timer rolls back with Health, so clients see the pawn dead from snapshots. It watches `StatusManager.HEALTH`. Design: pawn spec 8.7, 8.16.

### Constants

- `OWNED_TAGS_SOURCE = &"death"`: The name status.dead is added under in the pawn's [`OwnedTags`](../tags/REFERENCE.md#ownedtags).

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`DeathDefinition`](#deathdefinition).
- `is_timed() -> bool`: Timed: it runs while Health is 0.
- `run_length_ticks() -> int`
- `start() -> void`
- `can_sleep_while_running() -> bool`
- `tick(_dt: float) -> void`

## HitInfo

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/HitInfo.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

What one hit was, handed from the attacker to the target's `AbilityManager.receive_hit()`.

Plain data, made on the server only, where hits are decided. A hit carries effects, not numbers: the attacking ability's hit definition's effects say what it does, and the target's StatusManager applies them. A hit made in code gives its own, such as `Effect.make_damage(20)`. Design: pawn spec 8.6, 8.11.

### Settings and properties

- `attacker: Pawn` = `null`: Who hit.
- `attacker_id: int` = `-1`: The attacker's entity id, the same on every machine (instance id for a pawn not spawned through the session); -1 with none. For records and the network, which name pawns by entity id; nothing in the base reads it yet.
- `target: Pawn` = `null`: Who was hit.
- `ability: AbilityBase` = `null`: The ability that hit, such as a MeleeAttackAbility.
- `tick: int` = `0`: The tick the hit happened on.
- `direction: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: Flat, length 1: from the attacker toward the target. Knockback pushes this way.
- `effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: The effects that go on the target, in order.
- `attacker_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: The effects that go on the attacker once the hit lands (its hit definition's attacker_effects).
- `damage_dealt: float` = `0.0`: Filled in when the hit lands: how much Health it took, after resistances. 0 before then.

### Functions

- `make(attacker_pawn: Pawn, by: AbilityBase, target_pawn: Pawn, push_direction: Vector3, on_tick: int, target_effects: Effect[], self_effects: Effect[]) -> HitInfo` *(static)*: A hit by this ability on this target, carrying the ability's on-hit effects (or those given): what a swing and a projectile both make. attacker can be null (a projectile whose shooter is gone).
- `deliver() -> void`: Hands the hit to its target's AbilityManager (a pawn with no abilities can't be hit) and tells the ability it landed.
- `planned_damage() -> float`: The Health this hit's effects take before resistances, from their StatChangeEffectors. For readouts that show a hit before it lands.

## HitQuery

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/HitQuery.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Which pawns a hit volume touches this tick: one question for a swing's sweep and a projectile's flight (ability spec 13.1).

Spheres of one radius along a path (no more than half a radius apart, so nothing is skipped) against the pawns' capsules, nearest the path's start first. Inside: the C++ pawn grid, physics without it, and lag compensation when the attacker saw other pawns in the past. The history query and one batched call a tick for every volume come in here later, so melee and projectiles get them at once.

### Functions

- `touching(centres: PackedVector3Array, radius: float, tick: int, attacker: Pawn, view_ticks_behind: float = 0.0, include_attacker: bool = false) -> Pawn[]` *(static)*: The pawns these spheres touch on this tick, nearest the first centre first. The attacker is left out unless include_attacker. With view_ticks_behind above 0 and a session, as the attacker saw them (lag compensation).
- `line_centres(start: Vector3, end: Vector3, radius: float) -> PackedVector3Array` *(static)*: Spheres of this radius along the line start -> end, no more than half a radius apart so nothing between them is skipped: the centres for `touching()` for a projectile's flight or a hitscan line.
- `point_on_path(start: Vector3, end: Vector3, pawn: Pawn) -> Vector3` *(static)*: The point on the path start -> end nearest a pawn: where a hit on it is placed.

## HitRun

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/HitRun.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

What one hit volume has done: whom it hit, everything it met, and whether it's spent (ability spec 13.3). Shared by swings and projectiles.

A swing's run belongs to the run of its ability; a projectile owns one, so two bolts of a volley can each hit the same pawn. Each tick the volume hands it the pawns [`HitQuery`](#hitquery) found (and the world, if it met it): each pawn is met once, logged, checked against the [`HitDefinition`](#hitdefinition), and hit through `AbilityBase.land_hit()`. The hit list lives on its holder (an ability's rolled-back `AbilityBase.pawns_hit_this_run`, or a projectile's own), so a rollback restores it. The intersect log is packed arrays, for hooks and debugging, not rolled back.

### Settings and properties

- `hit: HitDefinition` = `null`: Who and what a hit does. Set by its owner, and swappable between ticks.
- `ability: AbilityBase` = `null`: The ability whose hits these are; land_hit goes through it. Null once it's gone: then pawns are met but not hit.
- `team: int` = `0`: The attacker's team, for the whitelist (kept, so a shooter that's gone still has one).
- `on_intersect: Callable`: Called with each log entry as it's made (a Dictionary, see `entry()`); the owner sends its own hook from it.
- `last_point: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: Where the meeting that spent it was.

### Constants

- `Kind.PAWN = 0`
- `Kind.WORLD = 1`
- `BODY_HEIGHT = 1.8`: How high a pawn's body is checked for the world check, in metres above its feet.

### Functions

- `_init(list_holder: Object = null, list_property: StringName = &"") -> void`: A run whose hit list is this property of holder (its owner keeps the list, and rolls it back if it should).
- `remember_source(source: AbilityBase) -> void`: Keeps what a hit needs if its source goes before it lands (the hit definition's lands_without_source): the hit definition's effects and the attacker's id. A projectile calls it as it sets off.
- `clear() -> void`: Starts again: no one met, nothing hit. A swing's run calls it when its ability starts; the hit list is cleared by its holder.
- `meet_pawns(pawns: Pawn[], tick: int, attacker: Pawn, path_start: Vector3, path_end: Vector3, motion: Vector3, reach_from: Variant = null) -> bool`: Handles the pawns a volume touched this tick, nearest first: each one met for the first time is logged and, if the hit definition allows, hit (path_start and path_end place meetings, motion gives the push, reach_from is where the world check starts; null: path_start). True once it's spent (max_hits or max_intersects): the caller stops there.
- `meet_world(tick: int, at: Vector3, normal: Vector3) -> bool`: Logs meeting the world here. Returns true if that spends it (max_intersects).
- `is_spent() -> bool`: True once it has hit max_hits pawns, or met max_intersects things.
- `hit_count() -> int`: How many pawns it has hit.
- `intersect_count() -> int`: How many things it has met.
- `entry(index: int) -> Dictionary`: One log entry: {"tick", "kind" (Kind), "target" (a Pawn or null), "key" (its id), "point", "normal" (the world's), "hit", "blocked" (the world was in the way)}.

## JumpAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/JumpAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

Jumping: an action bound to &"jump", which happens at once.

It starts from the ground, or within `coyote_ticks` of walking off an edge. A press a moment too early waits `buffer_window_ticks` and jumps on landing; holding the key doesn't bounce, because only a press starts it. Height comes from the pawn's JumpVelocity stat, in metres per second upward. Rollback: `left_ground_at`. Design: pawn spec 8.5.

### Settings and properties

- `left_ground_at: int` = `-4611686018427387904`: The last tick the pawn was known to be on the ground before it left it; `ON_GROUND` while it's there. Rolls back (pushed).

### Constants

- `ON_GROUND = -4611686018427387904`: `left_ground_at` while the pawn is on the ground.
- `COUNT_CAP = 100`: The most `ticks_off_ground()` counts. Anything past the coyote time counts the same.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`JumpDefinition`](#jumpdefinition).
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`
- `ticks_off_ground() -> int`: Ticks since the pawn was last on the ground, up to `COUNT_CAP`; 0 on the ground.
- `every_tick(_dt: float) -> void`
- `can_sleep() -> bool`: True while on the ground: a sleeping pawn is grounded, so it would only keep it there (pawn spec 15.3).
- `can_start() -> bool`
- `start() -> void`

## KnockbackAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/KnockbackAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

Being pushed by a hit: an action with no trigger action, started by `event.reaction.knockback`, which a [`KnockbackEffector`](../effects/REFERENCE.md#knockbackeffector) sends with the push ([`KnockbackEventData`](#knockbackeventdata)); code can push with `push()`.

It lives on the pawn being hit. For the push's duration it sets the pawn's horizontal velocity to the push, fading in a straight line to nothing, and locks out movement and combat. A push with a hop speed lifts a grounded pawn on its first tick (not one already in the air); the hop can outlast the push. A second hit while it runs starts it again with the new push. Only Dash cancels it.
Rollback: `push_velocity` and `push_ticks` roll back with its timer, so a corrected client replays the push. Design: pawn spec 8.6, 8.9.

### Settings and properties

- `push_velocity: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: The push at the start, in metres per second; its y is the hop speed upward. Rolls back (pushed).
- `push_ticks: int` = `0`: How many ticks this push lasts. Rolls back (pushed).

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`KnockbackDefinition`](#knockbackdefinition).
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`
- `is_timed() -> bool`: Timed, by its push's length rather than duration.
- `run_length_ticks() -> int`
- `prepare_from_event(event: GameplayEventData) -> void`: Takes the push from its event before it starts (its length decides how long it runs).
- `push(velocity: Vector3, ticks: int, hop: float = 0.0) -> bool`: Starts a push from code; hop is the upward speed in metres per second (0: none). Returns false if something stronger is running.
- `tick(_dt: float) -> void`

## KnockbackEventData

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/KnockbackEventData.gd`, extends [`GameplayEventData`](../entities/REFERENCE.md#gameplayeventdata)

What a knockback event carries: the push's start values (pawn spec 16.7).

A [`KnockbackEffector`](../effects/REFERENCE.md#knockbackeffector) sends it to the pawn it pushes as `event.reaction.knockback`, and the pawn's [`KnockbackAbility`](#knockbackability) starts from it, reading the push before it starts. instigator is who pushed; optional_object is the hit, if one did it.

### Settings and properties

- `push_velocity: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: The push at its start, flat, in metres per second.
- `push_ticks: int` = `0`: How many ticks the push lasts, at the match's rate.
- `hop_speed: float` = `0.0`: How fast it lifts a grounded pawn, in metres per second. 0: no hop.

## MeleeAttackAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/MeleeAttackAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

A melee swing: an action bound to &"primary", built from steps.

A swing is a [`WindupStep`](#windupstep) with a [`TurnToFaceStep`](#turntofacestep) beside it, a [`MeleeSweepStep`](#meleesweepstep) (the hit window), then an [`OpenComboStep`](#opencombostep) and a [`WaitStep`](#waitstep) for recovery. With no [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children of its own it makes those from the settings below, about 0.4 s with the defaults; place steps of your own for another pattern (these settings then only matter for `attack_range`, the AI's reach, and `warns_targets`). It locks out movement and other combat; Dash cancels it, Sprint and Jump don't. Hits happen on the server only, during the sweep, and a replay never hits again. What a hit does is its hit definition's effects (`AbilityDefinition.hit`), not the swing itself. Design: pawn spec 8.6, 8.9, 8.20.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`MeleeAttackDefinition`](#meleeattackdefinition).
- `attack_reach() -> float`: Its attack_range: the AI swings from within it.
- `start() -> void`
- `default_timeline() -> TimelineEntry[]`: The timeline for the steps it made: Windup and TurnToFace together, Sweep when the windup is done, then OpenCombo and Recovery. With steps of its own and no timeline in its definition, they run one after another.
- `swing_phase() -> Dictionary`: Where the swing is, for visuals: "windup", "hit" or "recovery" with progress 0 to 1 (smooth between ticks), or "none".
- `hit_offset_at(progress: float, facing: float) -> Vector3`: Where the hit sphere is at this point of the sweep, 0 (start) to 1 (end), as an offset from the pawn's feet for a facing in radians, so visuals draw the spots the hit checks. From `MeleeSweepStep.offset_at()`; straight ahead at chest height with no sweep.
- `windup_length() -> int`: Ticks the first windup lasts. It can take longer while it waits for the turn; `swing_phase()` says where it really is.
- `hit_length() -> int`: Ticks the first sweep can hit for.

## ParryAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/ParryAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

A parry stance: while it runs, a hit from the front does nothing to this pawn, and the attacker is pushed back instead.

This ability is the stance: it runs for duration (21 ticks, then a 90-tick cooldown), turns the pawn toward where it looks and holds it still. Parrying is its running effect's job: an effect granting status.parrying, holding a [`ParryModifier`](../effects/REFERENCE.md#parrymodifier) with the front's width and what the attacker gets (by default 120 degrees and nothing back), on the pawn while the stance lasts. Hits from the sides and back land as usual, and a knockback or a dash cancels the stance. A client sees its own stance at once; the parried hit's result arrives in snapshots. Design: pawn spec 8.15, 16.7.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`ParryDefinition`](#parrydefinition).
- `tick(dt: float) -> void`
- `guard() -> ParryModifier`: Its parry: the first [`ParryModifier`](../effects/REFERENCE.md#parrymodifier) in its running effects, or null. The debug drawing reads the front's width from it.
- `default_running_effects_now() -> Effect[]`: With no running effects of its own, a Parry parries 120 degrees wide, with nothing back.

## RangedAttackAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/RangedAttackAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

A ranged attack: an action bound to &"primary" that fires a projectile, built from steps.

A shot is a [`WindupStep`](#windupstep) with a [`TurnToFaceStep`](#turntofacestep) beside it, a [`FireProjectileStep`](#fireprojectilestep), then a [`WaitStep`](#waitstep) for recovery. With no [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children of its own it makes those from the settings below; place steps of your own for another pattern (a volley is several fire steps). It locks out movement and other combat while it runs; Dash cancels it. What a hit does is its hit definition's effects (`AbilityDefinition.hit`), carried by the projectile. Design: pawn spec 8.24.

```gdscript
# in a pawn's AbilityManager: a RangedAttack whose definition names a ProjectileDefinition and a hit with effects
pawn.ability_manager.can_start(&"primary")
```

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`RangedAttackDefinition`](#rangedattackdefinition).
- `attack_reach() -> float`: Its attack_range: the AI shoots from within it.
- `default_timeline() -> TimelineEntry[]`: The timeline for the steps it made: Windup and TurnToFace together, Fire when the windup is done, then Recovery. With steps of its own and no timeline in its definition, they run one after another.

## ReceiveHitAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/ReceiveHitAbility.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Taking a hit: an instant action, started by `event.hit.taken`, that decides what a hit does to its pawn (pawn spec 16.7).

The AbilityManager sends the event as a hit is delivered (on the server, after simulate), and this starts with the hit as its trigger data, in its own category, which nothing locks out. Its start requirements decide whether a hit counts at all: by default a pawn that owns status.hit_immune ignores it. Otherwise the hit arrives (`AbilityManager.hit_arrived`, so the AI notes the attack) and is either blocked (`AbilityManager.hit_blocked`: the pawn is dead, invulnerable, or parrying and facing the attacker, whose reply goes back on the next tick) or lands: the status manager applies its effects, `AbilityManager.hit_received` goes out, then the attacker gets its effects. A game changes what hits do by extending it. The manager adds one to a pawn without.

### Constants

- `BLOCKED_DEAD = &"dead"`: Why a hit was blocked, as `AbilityManager.hit_blocked` gives it.
- `BLOCKED_INVULNERABLE = &"invulnerable"`
- `BLOCKED_PARRIED = &"parried"`

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`ReceiveHitDefinition`](#receivehitdefinition).
- `start() -> void`
- `resolve(hit: HitInfo) -> void`: Resolves one hit on this pawn, on the server: it arrives, then it's blocked or it lands (see the class description).
- `blocked_by(hit: HitInfo) -> StringName`: Why this hit is blocked (one of the BLOCKED_ names), or &"" if it lands. A parry that blocks it sends its reply from here.

## SprintAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/SprintAbility.gd`, extends [`WalkAbility`](#walkability)

Running faster while a charge lasts: a locomotion ability bound to &"sprint".

It moves like Walk, at SprintSpeed. While &"sprint" is held and it has charge it runs instead of Walk. Sprinting drains the charge one tick per tick; `recharge_delay_ticks` after it stops, the charge refills at `recharge_rate`. It starts only with at least `min_start_charge_ticks`, so a held key on an empty charge doesn't flicker it on a tick at a time. An AI uses it by holding &"sprint".
The charge is worked out from two values set only when it starts or stops (`charge_at_switch`, `switched_at`), so nothing changes while it drains or refills (ability spec 4). `ready_at` is the tick the charge reaches the minimum, so the manager and the AI see when it can start again. Design: pawn spec 8.5.

### Settings and properties

- `charge_at_switch: int` = `0`: Ticks of charge when it last started or stopped. Rolls back (pushed).
- `switched_at: int` = `-1`: The tick it last started or stopped; -1: never, so the charge is full. Rolls back (pushed).

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`SprintDefinition`](#sprintdefinition).
- `charge_ticks() -> int`: Ticks of sprinting it has now: draining while it runs, refilling while it doesn't. Worked out from the tick.
- `is_timed() -> bool`
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`
- `run_length_ticks() -> int`
- `start() -> void`
- `stop() -> void`
- `delay_run(ticks: int) -> void`

## WalkAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/WalkAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

Walking on the ground: accelerating, slowing, steering in the air and turning to face where it's going. The default locomotion.

Its numbers come from the pawn's stats, so a buff or a different pawn changes them: `speed_stat` (MoveSpeed), Acceleration, Deceleration, AirControl and TurnRate (degrees per second), each with a fallback for a pawn without it. The pawn adds gravity. While its category is locked out (an attack that roots the pawn) it stops steering and the pawn slows to a stop. Design: pawn spec 8.5.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`WalkDefinition`](#walkdefinition).
- `tick(dt: float) -> void`

## AbilityDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/AbilityDefinition.gd`, extends [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition)

The settings one variant of an ability has, shared by every pawn that uses it, such as "Goblin Swing": a Resource an ability node points at (ability spec 3).

Each kind of ability has its own class with its settings added ([`MeleeAttackDefinition`](#meleeattackdefinition)); a new one starts with the kind's defaults. Variants (`Definition.based_on`) come from [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition). Read-only while playing: every pawn using it shares it. A pawn that needs other numbers uses another definition (`AbilityBase.use_definition()`), or gets them from stats and effects.

### Settings and properties

- `trigger_action: StringName` = `&""`: The named action that starts it, such as &"jump". Empty: only the manager starts it, as the default locomotion.
- `trigger_event: StringName` = `&""`: The gameplay event that starts it (`Tags.EVENT`), by the same rules as a press: event.health.depleted for Death, event.hit.taken for the hit ability. The event's data is the ability's `AbilityBase.trigger_data` as it starts (the hit, a push). Empty: no event starts it.
- `category: StringName` = `&""`: What it is, as a tag such as &"ability.movement.jump". Used for lockouts. Empty: nothing can lock it out.
- `extra_categories: StringName[]` = `[]`: More groups it belongs to besides category, such as &"ability.movement.advanced" for a dash. Lockouts, cancels and `AbilityManager.action_for_tag()` answer to all of them. They share one 64-bit mask with every other ability tag.
- `priority: int` = `0`: Which ability a press picks among those on one action: the highest that can start wins, then the first in the tree. Locomotion with a held action works the same. Effects can add to it (AbilityModifier, pawn spec 8.11).
- `combo_positions: int[]` = `[]`: Which combo positions it can fill: [1] an opener, [2] a second hit, [2, 3] second or third. A follow-up (no 1) starts only while the combo window is open; give it a higher priority than the opener so it wins there. Empty: not in combos. Pawn spec 8.20.
- `priority_jitter: float` = `0.0`: A random offset, up to plus or minus this, added to priority when a press picks between abilities. 0: none. It comes from the tick's own random numbers ([`DeterministicRandom`](../singletons/REFERENCE.md#deterministicrandom)), so a replay picks the same ability. Locomotion ignores it.
- `duration_ticks: int` = `0`: How long it runs, in ticks at 60 a second. For an action, 0 means it happens at once. For locomotion, 0 means it runs as long as it's wanted.
- `cooldown_ticks: int` = `0`: Ticks at 60 a second after it stops before it can start again.
- `locks_out: StringName[]` = `[]`: Categories that can't start, or steer, while this runs, such as &"ability.movement" for an attack that roots the pawn.
- `buffer_window_ticks: int` = `0`: Ticks at 60 a second a press waits if the ability can't start yet, such as jump pressed just before landing. 0: a press is tried once.
- `interrupt_priority: int` = `0`: How hard it cancels a running ability it conflicts with (pawn spec 8.6): Walk 0, Jump 5, Sprint 10, Parry 10, MeleeAttack 15, Knockback 30, Dash 40, Death 1000.
- `interrupt_threshold: int` = `100`: While it runs, a conflicting ability with at least this interrupt_priority cancels it; a weaker one is locked out. 100: only Death cancels it. MeleeAttack uses 15, so Dash cancels a swing and Sprint doesn't.
- `cancelled_by: StringName[]` = `[]`: Categories that can always cancel it while it runs, whatever the interrupt numbers say, such as &"ability.movement.jump". A category covers its children, as in locks_out.
- `pauses_locomotion: bool` = `false`: On: locomotion (Walk, Sprint) doesn't run at all while this does, so it neither steers nor slows the pawn (Dash). Off: a locked-out locomotion still slows the pawn to a stop, as an attack that roots the pawn wants.
- `needs_full_movement: bool` = `false`: On: while it runs the pawn moves by physics (`move_and_slide`), not the CrowdMover, so fast or forced moves such as Dash and Knockback collide properly. Pawn spec 8.22.
- `start_requirements: TagQuery`: Tags the pawn must own (all of, any of) and must not own (none of) for it to start, such as none of status.stunned. Only tags clients own too (ability, effect, status): the AI's own tags (ai.*) are owned only on the server, so a client would predict a start that doesn't happen. Empty: no tag rule.
- `max_charges: int` = `0`: Limited uses: how many times it can start before it has to wait for charges to come back. 0: no limit. The ability's own value can be changed while playing, for good or for a while (`AbilityBase.set_max_charges()`, `AbilityBase.add_max_charges_change()`).
- `recharges: bool` = `false`: On: spent charges come back on their own, every charge_restore_ticks. Off: only a refill gives them back (revive, a reload).
- `charge_restore_ticks: int` = `600`: With recharges on: while any charges are spent, some come back every this many ticks (at 60 a second), counted from the first one spent.
- `charges_restored: int` = `1`: How many charges come back each time. Ignored when restore_all_charges is on.
- `restore_all_charges: bool` = `false`: On: each restore gives back every spent charge, a full magazine.
- `has_charges_tag: StringName` = `&""`: A tag the pawn owns while this ability has charges left (always, with no limit), such as status.has_ammo.ranged: what the AI's Keep Distance asks for. Empty: none.
- `start_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: Effects on its own pawn when it starts (a combo boost), on every machine that runs it, rollback replays included, so an over-time one is predicted; their effectors fire on the authority only (pawn spec 16.7).
- `running_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: Effects on its own pawn while it runs: applied as it starts (after start_effects) and removed as it ends, whatever their duration (a parry's stance, a dash's invulnerability). One meant to last the whole run has lasts_until_removed on. Empty: its kind's default (Dash: invulnerable for its first 11 ticks; Parry: parrying, 120 degrees wide). Only for an ability that runs for a while.
- `hit: HitDefinition`: Who its hits may hit and what they do (ability spec 13.2), for its swings and its projectiles: its target_effects and attacker_effects are what a hit does. Empty: its kind's default (a swing hits enemies, doing nothing; a ranged attack's projectile stops at the first). A sweep step or a timeline entry can name another.
- `step_timeline: TimelineEntry[]` = `[]`: For a stepped ability: when each step runs (ability spec 6.2), as entries in ticks from its start. Empty: its kind's default (a swing's windup, sweep and recovery), or its steps one after another.
- `max_steps_ticks: int` = `600`: For a stepped ability, the longest it can run, in ticks at 60 a second. It ends when no step runs, or at this. Ignored without steps.

## HitDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/HitDefinition.gd`, extends [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition)

Who a hit may hit and what it does, for a swing and a projectile alike (ability spec 13.2).

An ability's definition holds one (`AbilityDefinition.hit`); a sweep step or a ranged attack's projectile can name another, and an ability can swap it while playing (`AbilityBase.use_hit_definition()`). Variants come from [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition). It matters only where hits are decided, so it needs no id on the wire.

### Settings and properties

- `hits_self: bool` = `false`: On: it can hit its own pawn (a projectile once it has left the shooter's body).
- `hits_allies: bool` = `false`: On: it can hit pawns on the attacker's team.
- `hits_enemies: bool` = `true`: On: it can hit pawns on other teams.
- `target_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: Effects on a pawn it hits, in order: damage, knockback, a slow (pawn spec 16.7).
- `attacker_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: Effects on the attacker when it lands (a boost for landing a blow).
- `push: int` = `0`: Which way a hit pushes its target.
- `max_hits: int` = `0`: The most pawns one run of it hits (a swing's run, or one projectile): a projectile stops there, a swing hits no one else. 0: no limit.
- `blocked_by_world: bool` = `true`: On: the world can block a hit (ability spec 13.8), checked along the weapon's reach rather than from the chest, so a wall stops a swing but a low crate it passes over doesn't. Two short rays per pawn hit; a projectile's flight already stops at the world.
- `world_mask: int` = `1`: The physics layers that block it. Leave a layer out to let hits through what's on it (a thin wooden wall).
- `lands_without_source: bool` = `false`: On: a hit still lands when its source is gone (a removed shooter's fireball), with the effects it had when it set off and credit to the attacker's id. Off: a source that's gone lands nothing. A removed pawn usually lingers until its projectiles end anyway (`NetworkEntity.linger_until_tick`), so this is for a source that can't.
- `max_intersects: int` = `0`: Ends it after this many intersects of any kind (pawns it may or may not hit, the world). 0: no limit.

### Constants

- `Push.FROM_ATTACKER = 0`: away from the attacking pawn (a swing)
- `Push.ALONG_MOTION = 1`: the way the hit volume was moving (a projectile's flight)

### Functions

- `allows(attacker: Pawn, target: Pawn, attacker_team: int) -> bool`: True if the whitelist lets it hit this pawn, attacked by that one (null: no attacker, so only the team rules apply).
- `push_direction(from: Vector3, target_position: Vector3, motion: Vector3) -> Vector3`: The direction a hit pushes: away from the attacker's position, or along the motion.

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/JumpDefinition.gd`, extends [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition)

A new one starts with the kind's defaults; see [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition) for variants. The Jump node reads it.

### Settings and properties

- `coyote_ticks: int` = `6`: Ticks at 60 a second after leaving the ground, without jumping, that a press still jumps.

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/KnockbackDefinition.gd`, extends [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition)

## MeleeAttackDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/MeleeAttackDefinition.gd`, extends [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition)

A melee attack's settings: its timings, reach and sweep.

A new one starts with the kind's defaults; see [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition) for variants. The MeleeAttack node reads it.

### Settings and properties

- `windup_ticks: int` = `8`: Ticks from the start of the swing to when it can hit (its Windup step's length).
- `hit_ticks: int` = `4`: Ticks it can hit for (its Sweep step's length).
- `recovery_ticks: int` = `12`: Ticks after hitting before it's over (its Recovery step's length).
- `attack_range: float` = `1.8`: How far it reaches, in metres from the pawn: the far edge of the hit sphere.
- `hit_radius: float` = `0.8`: The hit sphere's radius, in metres.
- `hit_height: float` = `1.0`: The hit sphere's height above the pawn's feet, in metres: about the chest.
- `sweep_degrees: float` = `100.0`: How far round the hit sphere sweeps during the hit ticks, in degrees, centred straight ahead. 0: it holds still.
- `sweep_from_left: bool` = `false`: On: the sweep goes from the pawn's left to its right. Off: right to left.
- `height_at_sweep_start: float` = `0.0`: How far above or below hit_height the sphere is at the start of the sweep, in metres: slashes, rises, chops. 0: level.
- `height_at_sweep_end: float` = `0.0`: The same at the end of the sweep. Between the two the sphere moves in a straight line up or down.
- `sweep_keys: SweepKey[]` = `[]`: The swing's path as keys (ability spec 7): points it goes through, in order of their time, measured from the pawn. Fewer than two: the arc from the settings above (sweep_degrees and the heights). A weapon's path baked from its animation goes here.
- `windup_turn_degrees_per_second: float` = `-1.0`: Degrees per second it turns toward where the pawn looks (its TurnToFace step). -1: the pawn's TurnRate stat (540 without one). 0: no turning.
- `combo_window_ticks: int` = `30`: How long the combo window stays open after its hit, in ticks at 60 a second (its OpenCombo step).
- `warns_targets: bool` = `true`: On: when a swing starts (server), enemies within reach and in front are told it's coming, so their AI can parry. One sphere query.

## ParryDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/ParryDefinition.gd`, extends [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition)

A parry's settings.

A new one starts with the kind's defaults; see [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition) for variants. The Parry node reads it.

### Settings and properties

- `turn_degrees_per_second: float` = `900.0`: How fast it turns toward where the pawn looks while it runs, in degrees per second. 0: it doesn't turn.

## ProjectileDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/ProjectileDefinition.gd`, extends [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition)

A projectile's flight, shared by every shot that uses it (ability spec 9): its speed and how it changes, how much it drops, its size, how far and long it flies, whether the world stops it, and its look. Who it may hit and what a hit does is its ability's [`HitDefinition`](#hitdefinition) (ability spec 13).

The one thing a designer makes for a new projectile: a ranged attack's definition names it (`RangedAttackDefinition.projectile_definition`), and the built-in projectile carries the networking. Variants come from [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition). Save it as a file in a registry folder, so clients find it by its index.

### Settings and properties

- `hitscan: bool` = `false`: On: hitscan. Everything along a straight line to its range is checked on the tick it's fired, as the shooter saw it, and clients draw a tracer for `tracer_seconds`. Speed, the speed curve and gravity don't apply.
- `tracer_seconds: float` = `0.1`: With hitscan: how long its tracer shows, from the muzzle to where it ended.
- `speed: float` = `30.0`: Metres a second at launch (times the speed curve's first value).
- `speed_curve: Curve`: How its speed changes over its flight: across, 0 to 1 through its lifetime; up, a multiplier on `speed`. Empty: steady. A rocket rises, an arrow falls away. Gravity's drop comes on top.
- `gravity_scale: float` = `0.0`: How much it drops, as a share of the world's gravity (physics/3d/default_gravity): 0 flies straight, 1 falls like a stone, 2 feels heavy. Tuning for how weighty it reads, not physics.
- `radius: float` = `0.15`: Radius of the hit sphere swept along its path, in metres.
- `max_range: float` = `40.0`: Metres it can fly before it's gone.
- `max_lifetime_ticks: int` = `180`: Ticks at 60 a second it can fly before it's gone.
- `hits_world: bool` = `true`: On: the level's solid geometry (world_mask) stops it.
- `world_mask: int` = `1`: The physics layers that stop it (the ground and walls). To let shots through some walls (wood, cloth, thin cover), put those on a physics layer of their own and leave it out here; a variant that includes it is a shot that can't go through (the usual way games handle it). With hitscan, the same.
- `visual_scene: PackedScene`: How it looks in flight: any scene (a mesh, particles, a trail), turned to face along its flight (-Z forward). Empty: nothing is drawn, but it still flies and hits.
- `impact_scene: PackedScene`: Spawned where it ends, on a pawn or the world, on every machine that draws it: a spark, a puff of dust. Its own node in the world, not part of the projectile, and a visual: it isn't sent, so a gameplay effect (an explosion that hurts) belongs in a hit's effects.
- `impact_seconds: float` = `2.0`: Seconds an impact stays before it's freed (0: it frees itself).

### Functions

- `drop_per_second_squared() -> float`: Its drop in metres a second squared: the world's gravity times `gravity_scale`.
- `tracer_ticks() -> int`: With hitscan: the ticks its tracer shows.
- `lifetime_ticks() -> int`: How many ticks it flies before its lifetime is up, at the match's rate.
- `offset_at(direction: Vector3, age: float) -> Vector3`: Where it is this many ticks after launch (a fraction is between ticks), from its launch point, fired along direction (length 1). Worked out, not stepped, so every machine gets the same point for the same tick.
- `velocity_at(direction: Vector3, age: float) -> Vector3`: Its velocity this many ticks after launch, fired along direction (length 1).
- `speed_at(age: float) -> float`: Its speed along its direction this many ticks after launch: `speed` times the curve.
- `distance_at(age: float) -> float`: Metres flown along its direction this many ticks after launch.
- `spawn_impact(parent: Node, at: Vector3) -> void`: Spawns its impact scene at this point, under parent: a node of its own in the world, not a child of the projectile, which lives on after the projectile is gone and frees itself after `impact_seconds`.

## RangedAttackDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/RangedAttackDefinition.gd`, extends [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition)

A ranged attack's settings: its projectile, timings and muzzle.

A new one starts with the kind's defaults; see [`AbilityDefinition`](#abilitydefinition) for variants. The RangedAttack node reads it.

### Settings and properties

- `projectile_scene: PackedScene`: For a projectile with code of its own (homing, splitting): a scene whose root extends [`Projectile`](#projectile), with a TickStateComponent and a NetworkEntity, registered at startup (`Projectile.register_scene()`). Empty: the built-in projectile, flown by `projectile_definition`.
- `projectile_definition: ProjectileDefinition`: What it fires: speed, arc, size, hits, and how it looks ([`ProjectileDefinition`](#projectiledefinition)). A definition file, so clients can find it by its registry index.
- `windup_ticks: int` = `12`: Ticks of aiming before the shot, at 60 a second.
- `recovery_ticks: int` = `18`: Ticks after the shot before it's over, at 60 a second.
- `attack_range: float` = `14.0`: How far away a target may be for the AI to shoot, in metres (the AI's reach; the projectile's own range can be longer).
- `muzzle_below_eyes: float` = `0.3`: Where the projectile leaves from: metres below the pawn's eyes (`Pawn.eye_height`). The shot is aimed at the point the look meets, so it lands where the pawn looks.
- `muzzle_forward: float` = `0.5`: How far in front of the pawn the projectile starts, in metres.
- `windup_turn_degrees_per_second: float` = `-1.0`: How fast it turns toward its aim during the windup, degrees a second; -1 uses the pawn's TurnRate stat.
- `warns_targets: bool` = `true`: On: the first enemy on the projectile's path hears it's coming, so its AI can parry.
